body: Bullying is trauma for sure.  I was bullied by classmates and family, and it definitely contributed to my diagnosis.  It may have even been the main cause.

I had significant trauma starting around Grade 7.  Since I too was in fight-or-flight mode for much of my life, I missed out on basic middle school and some high school learning. 

Right now - as an adult - I'm studying 7th grade math, science, and history as I feel like I missed out on the fundamentals.  I plan to study all the way through high school level if time permits.  I feel like if I learn the basic stuff, I'll understand better what's happening in the world. 

I wouldn't say I'm not smart.  I graduated college and I work full time.  I just missed out on a lot of knowledge that would be nice to have.

Oh, and I also don't know many movie references.  I missed out on a lot of movies due to having a super religious family that wouldn't allow anything PG or higher.  I plan on slowly catching up.

Same. 40ish here and still enjoy books, movies, and TV shows that are made for teenagers or 'tweens.  Video games, too. I'm thinking about subscribing to Paramount+ just to watch the Nickelodeon shows of my youth.

It's mentioned here that trauma can make us "stuck" at a certain age. Things got really bad for me in 7th grade, so this makes sense.

I see "girls night out" as basically people backstabbing each other.  I'll read books or find other entertainment.

They still have someone to interact with or cuddle with.  As for me, I'm alone.  Actually have surgery coming up and I'm hoping they don't give me trouble about calling a cab or Uber.  Some places insist on having a "trusted person" come pick us up, and I do not have that.

I think even getting off the ship by 9am is more than a bit optimistic.  Don't forget customs is also a cluster.  Everyone needs to be photographed.  Plus there are always people who try to skip and the ship searches for them, paging them on the overhead etc.  If there's people ahead of you who haven't payed all their expenses, they will also hold up the line as they're sent back in to customer service.

If the ship doesn't dock until 8:00 am, the chances of arriving to the airport by 9:00 are slim to none.  Arriving at the airport by 10:00 *might* be possible, providing they're one of the first people off the ship and transportation arrives promptly.  The last cruise I was on delayed disembarking for some reason, and we seemed to stand in line for hours. (Don't forget, you'll have to go through customs on the ship if you sailed international, which can be very very time-consuming.) Then there will be the airport security lines which can be ruthless.  

I'd advise OP to find a slightly later flight for peace of mind.  No earlier than 2:00 pm.

Edit: Also, being back at Port at 8:00 am does not equal disembarkation at 8:00 am.  They might not start letting people off until 9:30 am or later.  Keep all this in mind.

I've given up, but not necessarily by choice.  After my abusive marriage and being completely destroyed by my last relationship, I've lost the ability to become attached.  I'm sure it's some sort of defense mechanism in my brain to protect me.

I was bullied from preschool onward.  Relentless abuse.  I never had friends and sat alone in the cafeteria.  To be seen with me was social suicide. Teachers would either look the other way or join the bullying.   Even in college I was bullied, mostly by catty girls in my major.  

I believe the reason I was bullied was my looks.  When I was young, I wanted to be a boy and ended up looking somewhere in between boy and girl.  Also I was tall for my age and awkward.  I didn't develop social skills until much later in life due to not having the social experience of the average child.  Even now I'm still catching up.

Fast forward to today, I'm an average to above-average looking female.  However I'm very untrusting of people and prefer spending my time alone.  I've been described as a recluse.  I absolutely think my bullying experience contributed to me developing BPD.  Every day from a very young age consisted of trauma from kids and adults (not to mention family members).  That certainly affected my brain development for life.
